correctness.rationale: Away from zeros and origin, Fock-Chern criticality gives (r²-n)z^n=a r², forcing all stationary points onto 2n rays. At zeros the quadratic positive expansion gives nondegenerate minima; origin n>=3 has negative definite quadratic term. On positive rays the radius solution r>sqrt(n) is unique and a radial maximum/angular minimum (saddle); on negative rays g(r)=(n-r²)r^(n-2) rises then falls with unique maximum at sqrt(n-2) and value A_n, making inner saddles and outer maxima for a<A_n, a degenerate tangency at equality and none above. H_outer/H_0 comparison reduces to ne^(-s/2)/(n-s), strictly increasing from below 1 to infinity on (n-2,n), so uniquely defines G_n. Independent numerical scalar root checks for n=3 through 20 corroborate G_n<A_n; the general proof is monotonicity, not sampling.
